Guideline: Detect the Blazor hosting model first
Description: Blazor Web App, standalone WebAssembly, Blazor Server and MAUI Hybrid have different rendering, styling and lifecycle rules; inspect .csproj, Program.cs and App.razor before designing
Do: Read the target framework, the Blazor SDK and Program.cs before proposing a layout or component
Don't: Assuming a React/Vue structure or a single Blazor hosting model for every project
Code Bad: Adding @rendermode to components in a project that has no Blazor Web App endpoints

Guideline: Choose the render mode per component
Description: Blazor Web Apps support Static SSR, Interactive Server, Interactive WebAssembly and Interactive Auto at component and page level
Do: Set @rendermode on the smallest interactive boundary and keep static content static
Don't: Marking the whole app interactive or copying a render mode without checking the requirement
Code Bad: @rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly repeated on every leaf component without reason

Guideline: Prefer static SSR for content-first pages
Description: Static server rendering ships no circuit and no WebAssembly payload, which keeps marketing, documentation and catalog pages fast
Do: Use static SSR for read-only pages and add interactive islands only where input is needed
Don't: Making every page interactive because a single widget needs JavaScript
Code Good: A static catalog page with one interactive search component
Code Bad: <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveServer" /> for the entire application

Guideline: Use Interactive Server for internal business apps
Description: Interactive Server keeps component state on the server over a SignalR circuit; ideal for intranets, ERP and admin dashboards with large server-owned data
Do: Keep the circuit payload small and design for reconnection
Don't: Choosing Interactive Server for a public high-traffic site without capacity planning
Code Good: App.razor keeps static SSR and only the workspace layout is InteractiveServer
Code Bad: Every public marketing page uses InteractiveServer by default

Guideline: Use Interactive WebAssembly only when the client needs it
Description: WebAssembly rendering runs in the browser after downloading the app; justified by offline work, client-side computation or server-free hosting
Do: Budget the download, show a first-load experience and keep the server API small
Don't: Moving an entire data-heavy dashboard to WebAssembly without measuring startup cost
Code Good: @rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly on an offline editor route
Code Bad: InteractiveWebAssembly for a simple form that posts to the server anyway

Guideline: Use Interactive Auto for fast first paint with rich interaction
Description: Interactive Auto starts on the server and switches to WebAssembly on later visits, trading a larger download for repeat-visit speed
Do: Use it for public apps where both first load and rich interaction matter, and verify both phases
Don't: Treating Auto as a free upgrade without testing the WebAssembly phase or its API dependencies
Code Good: @rendermode InteractiveAuto on a customer portal page
Code Bad: Auto render mode on pages that require server-only services with no client equivalent

Guideline: Plan for prerendering and double initialization
Description: Interactive components are prerendered by default, so OnInitializedAsync can run twice and JavaScript interop is unavailable during prerender
Do: Guard data loading, tolerate repeated initialization and move DOM work to OnAfterRenderAsync
Don't: Mutating the DOM in OnInitializedAsync or assuming a single initialization pass
Code Good: protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync() { if (_items is null) _items = await LoadAsync(); }
Code Bad: Calling IJSRuntime in OnInitializedAsync and expecting the browser to exist

Guideline: Keep shared components render-mode agnostic
Description: A component library reused by server, WebAssembly and MAUI projects must not depend on one host's services
Do: Depend on abstractions and pass data through parameters; keep host services at the page boundary
Don't: Injecting a server-only DbContext into a shared Razor class library component
Code Good: Component takes IReadOnlyList<Order> and EventCallback<Order> parameters
Code Bad: Shared component injects AuthenticationStateProvider and a SQL DbContext directly

Guideline: Do not apply Web App render modes to MAUI Hybrid
Description: MAUI Blazor Hybrid always renders interactively inside a WebView; render modes, circuits and WebAssembly startup do not apply
Do: Use the MAUI Hybrid profile for safe areas, touch, native navigation and offline data
Don't: Adding @rendermode attributes or circuit reconnection UI to a MAUI project
Code Good: Hybrid page inherits layout and uses MAUI device services through DI
Code Bad: @rendermode InteractiveServer inside a MAUI BlazorWebView page

Guideline: Migrate legacy Blazor Server hosting to a Blazor Web App
Description: Pre-.NET 8 Blazor Server uses Startup.cs, _Host.cshtml and MapBlazorHub; the Blazor Web App model replaces these with Program.cs and component render modes
Do: Move routing into Routes.razor and host markup into App.razor
Don't: Mixing _Host.cshtml, Startup.cs and render modes in a new .NET 8+ project
Code Bad: app.UseEndpoints(endpoints => endpoints.MapBlazorHub()); inside Startup.Configure in a .NET 10 app

Guideline: Use the legacy circuit handler pattern only on old Blazor Server
Description: Pre-.NET 8 apps track connections with CircuitHandler implementations and a scoped circuit accessor, not with the component-scoped services available today
Do: Keep CircuitHandler in legacy apps and register it as scoped
Don't: Copying legacy circuit tracking into a Blazor Web App without checking the supported replacement
Code Bad: Static mutable circuit counters shared across users

Guideline: Split pages into small focused Razor components
Description: Extract layout regions, toolbar, filters, data grid, dialogs and empty states into named components instead of one giant page
Do: One responsibility per component with parameters and events at the boundary
Don't: A 600-line Dashboard.razor that mixes querying, layout and formatting
Code Bad: @foreach inside Dashboard.razor with inline formatting, filtering and dialog markup

Guideline: Put logic in code-behind files
Description: A .razor.cs partial class keeps markup readable and makes logic unit-testable
Do: Use partial class Dashboard : ComponentBase in Dashboard.razor.cs for data access and handlers
Don't: Business logic, HTTP calls and validation compiled into @code blocks of the page markup
Code Bad: @code { /* 200 lines of repository calls */ }

Guideline: Treat parameters as immutable inputs
Description: Blazor reuses parameter objects; mutating them breaks change detection and surprises the parent
Do: Copy parameters into local state inside OnParametersSet
Don't: Assigning to a [Parameter] inside the component
Code Good: private string _name = string.Empty; protected override void OnParametersSet() => _name = Name;
Code Bad: [Parameter] public string Name { get; set; } = ""; void Rename() => Name = "x";

Guideline: Raise events with EventCallback and EventCallback<T>
Description: EventCallback lets a parent handle child events without the child knowing the parent, and keeps StateHasChanged correct in every render mode
Do: Expose EventCallback<T> parameters and await them
Don't: Passing Action delegates or mutating parent state from the child directly
Code Bad: public Action<Item> OnSelect { get; set; } with parent state mutated in the child

Guideline: Use CascadingValue for theme and layout context
Description: Cascading parameters pass design tokens, density and direction to deep component trees without prop drilling
Do: Cascade a typed ThemeContext and subscribe only where needed
Don't: Cascading a dozen unrelated values or using globals instead of DI
Code Bad: Passing the same theme object through five component parameters

Guideline: Build generic components with @typeparam
Description: Generic components give typed tables, selects and lists without duplicating markup per model
Do: Use @typeparam TItem with RenderFragment<TItem> columns and a RowKey selector
Don't: Copy-pasting the same grid for every entity type
Code Good: @typeparam TItem; [Parameter] public IEnumerable<TItem> Items { get; set; }
Code Bad: OrderGrid.razor, CustomerGrid.razor and InvoiceGrid.razor with identical markup

Guideline: Key repeated items with @key
Description: Without @key Blazor reuses component instances positionally, leaking focus and state between rows
Do: Add @key with a stable identifier in lists, grids and editable rows
Don't: Relying on implicit order in filtered or reordered collections
Code Bad: @foreach (var row in Rows) { <OrderRow Item="row" /> } with editable inputs

Guideline: Inject services with @inject
Description: Constructor injection and @inject both resolve from the component's scope; register services explicitly in Program.cs
Do: Inject narrow interfaces and keep component dependencies few
Don't: Resolving services from a static provider or new-ing repositories in the component
Code Bad: var service = new OrderService(new SqlConnection(...)); inside a component

Guideline: Dispose subscriptions and interop handles
Description: Components that subscribe to events, timers, NavigationManager or JS modules must release them or the circuit/page leaks
Do: Implement IDisposable or IAsyncDisposable and dispose JS object references
Don't: Leaving NavigationManager.LocationChanged subscriptions attached after navigation
Code Good: @implements IAsyncDisposable; public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await _module.DisposeAsync();
Code Bad: SubscribeLocationChanged in OnInitialized without ever unsubscribing

Guideline: Bind with @bind-Value and choose the update event
Description: Two-way binding works with @bind and @bind-Value; the default onchange event fires on blur
Do: Use @bind:event="oninput" for search, and onchange for validation-heavy fields
Don't: Rebinding every keystroke to an expensive server call
Code Bad: <input value="@_query" @onchange="e => _query = e.Value?.ToString()" /> for every field

Guideline: Handle @onchange and @oninput with typed event args
Description: Blazor event handlers receive ChangeEventArgs and FocusEventArgs; cast the value explicitly and never use string concatenation for identifiers
Do: Use @onchange with e.Value and @onkeydown for keyboard interaction
Don't: Assuming jQuery-style DOM access or calling preventDefault without @onkeydown:preventDefault
Code Bad: onchange="roleChanged(this)" JavaScript handler on a Blazor-owned element

Guideline: Render markup with @if and @foreach, never HTML strings
Description: Razor composes components safely; string-built HTML bypasses encoding and component state
Do: Use @if, @foreach and RenderFragment for conditional and repeated UI
Don't: Building markup with string.Format or MarkupString for user data
Code Bad:
builder.Append("
" + order.Name + "
")

Guideline: Share namespaces with _Imports.razor
Description: Imports keep component files clean and make the design system components available everywhere
Do: Add shared component, model and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components namespaces to _Imports.razor
Don't: @using repeated in every page
Code Bad: @using MyApp.Components.DesignSystem at the top of 40 pages

Guideline: Use @ref only for focus and measurement
Description: Element references are an escape hatch for focus management, scroll position and measured dimensions
Do: Store a focus target with @ref and focus it in OnAfterRenderAsync
Don't: Using @ref to mutate text or classes that should be bound state
Code Bad: _searchInput.Value = "" to push state instead of binding

Guideline: Use NavLink with Match for active navigation
Description: NavLink applies the active class from routing state, including prefix matches for sections
Do: Set Match="NavLinkMatch.All" for exact links and Prefix for section roots
Don't: Hand-rolling active state with window.location in JavaScript
Code Bad: Orders computed from a manual URL string

Guideline: Avoid JavaScript template syntax in Razor files
Description: Blazor markup uses @ directives and components; JSX, Vue directives and Angular templates do not compile and confuse maintainers
Do: Express conditionals with @if and lists with @foreach
Don't: Writing className, v-if, ngIf or map() render callbacks in .razor files
Code Bad: Items.map(item => <Row item={item} />) inside a .razor file

Guideline: Inspect the project before adding a CSS framework
Description: Blazor templates ship Bootstrap; enterprise apps often add Tailwind, MudBlazor or Radzen; never assume a framework is installed
Do: Check wwwroot, App.razor, package references and _Layout before recommending a styling approach
Don't: Introducing Tailwind or Bootstrap alongside an existing design system
Code Good: Read App.razor link tags and .csproj PackageReference before styling
Code Bad: Adding tailwind.config.js to a MudBlazor project that already has a theme

Guideline: Scope component styles with .razor.css
Description: CSS isolation generates a unique attribute scope so component styles cannot leak into other pages
Do: Put layout and component styles in Component.razor.css
Don't: Global selectors in wwwroot/app.css that restyle every button in the app
Code Bad: app.css: div { padding: 16px; } affecting every component

Guideline: Define design tokens once in wwwroot/css
Description: CSS custom properties are the shared contract between native CSS, CSS isolation and component-library themes
Do: Ship tokens.css, link it from App.razor or index.html before app.css, and consume var(--color-primary) everywhere
Don't: Hard-coding hex values in component CSS or in .razor style attributes
Code Bad: <button style="background:#2563eb"> repeated across pages

Guideline: Use ::deep for child markup in isolated CSS
Description: ::deep pierces the CSS-isolation boundary when a component styles markup rendered by a child component
Do: Use ::deep only for the child's outer contract, documented in the component
Don't: Global overrides with !important because ::deep was unknown
Code Bad: !important on every library selector from app.css

Guideline: Implement light and dark themes with data attributes
Description: A data-theme attribute on html plus token overrides keeps themes declarative and SSR-friendly
Do: Swap tokens under [data-theme="dark"] and persist the choice server-side or in localStorage
Don't: Duplicating every component style for dark mode
Code Bad: .dark .card, .dark .table, .dark .button { ... } for every component

Guideline: Use CSS logical properties for RTL support
Description: padding-inline, margin-inline-start and border-inline-start mirror automatically for Arabic, Hebrew and Persian
Do: Use logical properties in tokens and component CSS
Don't: Hard-coded left/right padding and text-align that break when dir changes
Code Bad: .card { padding-left: 1rem; border-left: 2px solid #2563eb; }

Guideline: Prefer Flexbox, Grid and container queries
Description: Layout should respond to available space instead of fixed pixel widths or per-page media queries
Do: Use Grid for dashboards, Flexbox for toolbars and container queries for cards
Don't: Fixed 1200px containers and absolute positioning for enterprise layouts
Code Bad: .stats { width: 1200px; } with float-based columns

Guideline: Respect prefers-reduced-motion
Description: Enterprise apps must not animate against a user's motion preference, and CSS isolation does not exempt transitions
Do: Wrap non-essential transitions and keyframes in a reduced-motion media query
Don't: Long slides, parallax or looping animation with no opt-out
Code Bad: animation: slide-in 1.2s infinite on every notification

Guideline: Do not override a component library with broad !important rules
Description: Library themes exist for a reason; global overrides fight specificity and break on upgrade
Do: Customize the library theme API and scope unavoidable overrides to one component
Don't: app.css rules with !important targeting .mud-*, .rz-* or .e-* classes
Code Good: MudTheme palette customization instead of overriding .mud-button-root
Code Bad: .mud-button-root { background: red !important; } in app.css

Guideline: Build forms with EditForm and a model
Description: EditForm wires validation, submit and field state; ad-hoc @onclick handlers lose all of that
Do: Use EditForm Model with OnValidSubmit and an EditContext for advanced scenarios
Don't: POSTing with fetch or manually reading input values in @code
Code Bad: <form @onsubmit="() => Save(_name, _email)"> with manual field reads

Guideline: Use built-in input components with data annotations
Description: InputText, InputNumber, InputSelect, InputCheckbox and InputDate integrate validation and formatting
Do: Use DataAnnotationsValidator and required/range attributes on the model
Don't: Custom two-way binding with @oninput for every field or parsing strings by hand
Code Bad: <input type="number" @onchange="e => _qty = int.Parse(e.Value.ToString())" />

Guideline: Place validation messages beside their fields
Description: Field-level messages are faster to resolve and screen-reader discoverable; a summary alone hides which field failed
Do: Use ValidationMessage For and keep a ValidationSummary at the top for long forms
Don't: Showing only a toast or a single generic error banner
Code Bad:
One

Invalid input

at the bottom of a 20-field form

Guideline: Add custom validation through the validation system
Description: Custom rules belong in attributes or IValidatableObject so EditForm can display them like any other error
Do: Create a ValidationAttribute and register it on the model
Don't: Throwing exceptions or setting a bool error flag from the submit handler
Code Bad: if (date < DateTime.Today) { _error = "Invalid date"; return; }

Guideline: Disable and mark controls busy during submit
Description: Double submits duplicate orders and writes; the UI must show progress and block re-entry
Do: Track _isSaving, disable the submit button, show a progress indicator and restore state in finally
Don't: Fire-and-forget async handlers that leave the button clickable
Code Bad: <button @onclick="SaveAsync">Save</button> with no busy state

Guideline: Preserve user input when submission fails
Description: A failed save must keep the model and scroll position so the user can correct the problem
Do: Keep the bound model instance and surface a retryable error near the action
Don't: Recreating the model or reloading the page after a server error
Code Good: catch (ApiException ex) { _error = ex.Message; } while _model stays bound
Code Bad: NavigationManager.NavigateTo("/orders/new", forceLoad: true) on failure

Guideline: Warn before discarding unsaved changes
Description: NavigationLock intercepts internal navigation so long enterprise forms do not silently lose work
Do: Use NavigationLock with ConfirmExternalNavigation and a clear discard dialog
Don't: Relying on beforeunload alone, which never fires for Blazor internal navigation
Code Bad: window.onbeforeunload registered in index.html only

Guideline: Make validation errors accessible
Description: Errors must be announced and linked to their inputs, not just colored red
Do: Associate messages with the field, set aria-invalid and move focus to the summary on submit
Don't: Color-only error borders or messages that appear far from the field
Code Bad: <InputText class="error" /> with no message text

Guideline: Structure the app with Router, RouteView and layouts
Description: Routes.razor owns routing, MainLayout owns the shell and pages stay thin
Do: Define layouts with @layout and nested layouts for sections
Don't: Building a custom router or duplicating the shell inside every page
Code Bad: Every page re-renders its own sidebar and header markup

Guideline: Protect navigation with AuthorizeView and roles
Description: Hide navigation and actions the user cannot perform, and enforce the same rule on the server
Do: Use AuthorizeView Roles and [Authorize] on pages and APIs
Don't: Hiding a link as the only access control
Code Bad: if (user.IsInRole("Finance")) render link, with no server-side authorization

Guideline: Provide NotFound and NotAuthorized experiences
Description: Router's NotFound and AuthorizeRouteView's NotAuthorized slots keep error navigation inside the app shell
Do: Design branded not-found and no-permission pages with a way back
Don't: Blank pages, raw 404 text or redirect loops when access is denied
Code Bad: Returning a raw HTTP 403 body with no navigation or explanation

Guideline: Use NavigationManager for programmatic navigation
Description: NavigationManager keeps internal navigation inside the Blazor app; forceLoad is for full reloads only
Do: Call NavigateTo with a relative path and update query strings deliberately
Don't: Using window.location.href in JavaScript for internal links
Code Bad: IJSRuntime.InvokeVoidAsync("eval", "window.location='/orders/1'")

Guideline: Keep navigation responsive with a collapsible drawer
Description: Enterprise navigation must degrade to an overlay drawer with focus management on small screens
Do: Collapse the sidebar below 1024px, use a hamburger with aria-expanded and trap focus while open
Don't: A fixed 280px sidebar that consumes the mobile viewport
Code Good: <aside class="sidebar" data-collapsed="@_collapsed"> with a toggle button
Code Bad: A fixed sidebar with min-width in every viewport

Guideline: Show breadcrumbs for deep hierarchies
Description: Breadcrumbs give orientation in ERP and admin sections with nested resources
Do: Derive breadcrumbs from route data or a page-provided trail
Don't: Relying on browser back as the only way to understand location
Code Bad: A page title with no parent context in a five-level hierarchy

Guideline: Handle navigation differently in static SSR
Description: Static SSR pages navigate with full page requests; interactive state and dialogs do not survive
Do: Use normal links, server-side redirects and progressive-enhancement forms for static pages
Don't: Assuming an interactive circuit exists on every page of a Blazor Web App
Code Bad: Holding a filter dialog open across navigation on a static SSR page

Guideline: Design business apps as workspaces, not landing pages
Description: Internal tools need dense, scannable, task-oriented layouts; hero sections and marketing CTAs waste the viewport
Do: Start from the user's daily task: find, filter, act, confirm
Don't: Copying a landing-page hero and feature grid into an admin console
Code Good: Toolbar, filters, grid and detail panel filling the viewport
Code Bad: Full-width hero with a gradient and a Get Started button in an ERP

Guideline: Give dense dashboards a clear hierarchy
Description: KPI cards, trend charts and tables need typographic hierarchy and spacing, not decoration
Do: Use one primary metric per region, consistent card padding and restrained accent color
Don't: Rainbow KPI tiles, drop shadows on every card and icon overload
Code Good: Four KPI cards with label, value, trend and one accent
Code Bad: Twelve gradient cards with emoji icons and random colors

Guideline: Data grids need sorting, filtering, paging and saved views
Description: Enterprise users scan thousands of rows; grids must support server-side paging and persistent filter state
Do: Use the installed grid's server-side data source and show active filters as removable chips
Don't: Loading an entire table into memory or hiding filters behind undocumented syntax
Code Bad: SELECT * rendered client-side with no paging or filter feedback

Guideline: Support bulk selection with explicit scope
Description: Bulk actions on filtered sets are dangerous unless the scope is visible and confirmed
Do: Show the selected count, the filtered scope and a confirmation for destructive actions
Don't: Applying delete to all rows when a filter is active without telling the user
Code Good: 3 of 240 matching orders selected - Delete selected
Code Bad: Delete all rows after a filtered selection

Guideline: Communicate status with text and icon, never color alone
Description: Color-blind users and forced-colors mode must still distinguish success, warning and failure
Do: Pair semantic color with a label and an icon, and expose the state to assistive tech
Don't: A green dot with no text as the only indication of an active system
Code Bad: as the only status indicator

Guideline: Use detail panels for master-detail workflows
Description: Side panels keep the list context while a record is inspected or edited
Do: Use an inline panel on desktop and a full-screen dialog on mobile, with focus trapping
Don't: Navigating away from the list to view a record and losing filter state
Code Bad: Full page navigation for every row click with no way back to the same page

Guideline: Expose audit and activity context
Description: Business apps need to show who changed what and when, aligned with the active locale
Do: Show actor, localized timestamp and change summary in a timeline
Don't: Unlabeled raw IDs and UTC timestamps users cannot interpret
Code Bad: Modified by user 8f3a at 2026-11-22T04:12:00Z

Guideline: Gate actions by role and permission
Description: Navigation, buttons and bulk actions must reflect authorization, with server enforcement
Do: Render actions from a permission-aware component and re-check on the server
Don't: Showing every action and failing only after the user submits
Code Bad: A disabled-only UI that still allows a crafted API request

Guideline: Design empty, loading and error states
Description: Every data surface needs a skeleton, a first-use empty state and a retryable error state
Do: Render skeletons during load and a clear next action for empty results
Don't: A blank table body while loading and a raw exception string on failure
Code Good: @if (_loading) { <SkeletonTable /> } else if (_error is not null) { <RetryError OnRetry="LoadAsync" /> }
Code Bad: @if (_rows is null) { } with no loading or error feedback

Guideline: Adapt data grids instead of shrinking them
Description: Narrow viewports need column prioritization, card rows or horizontal scrolling with a sticky key column
Do: Define column priority, hide low-value columns and expose them in a detail view
Don't: Scaling a twelve-column desktop grid down to 375px
Code Bad: min-width: 1200px on the table inside a 375px viewport

Guideline: Use the project breakpoints and verify 375 to 1440
Description: Check 375, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440; layout shifts usually appear at 390 and 768
Do: Define breakpoints once as tokens or container queries and test the stated widths
Don't: Only testing the developer's 1920px monitor
Code Bad: A single desktop layout assumed to work everywhere

Guideline: Keep touch targets at least 44px and never hover-only
Description: Touch and keyboard users need reachable targets and visible actions without hover
Do: Give icon buttons 44x44 hit areas and keep row actions visible on touch
Don't: 24px icon buttons and actions revealed only on mouse hover
Code Bad: .icon-button { width: 24px; height: 24px; } with opacity 0 until :hover

Guideline: Adapt dialogs and sidebars for small screens
Description: Dialogs should become full-screen sheets and sidebars overlays below the tablet breakpoint
Do: Switch layout at 768px and restore focus to the trigger on close
Don't: A 900px modal that overflows a 390px phone
Code Bad: dialog { width: 900px; } on every device

Guideline: Start from semantic HTML before adding ARIA
Description: Buttons, headings, tables, labels and landmarks carry behavior and semantics that divs must recreate badly
Do: Use button, nav, main, table and label elements, and add ARIA only to fill gaps
Don't: Clickable divs and icon-only links with no accessible name
Code Bad: x

Guideline: Manage focus in dialogs and drawers
Description: Focus must enter the dialog, stay inside while open and return to the trigger on close
Do: Trap focus, set initial focus on the first meaningful control and restore on close
Don't: Opening a modal with focus left on the page behind it
Code Bad: Displaying a fixed overlay with no focus change

Guideline: Support full keyboard operation for menus and grids
Description: Menus, comboboxes and grids need arrow keys, Home/End, Escape and visible focus
Do: Use the library's keyboard support or implement roving tabindex
Don't: Making a custom dropdown clickable only with the mouse
Code Bad:
Menu
with no key handling

Guideline: Announce asynchronous changes politely
Description: Grid reloads, save results and validation summaries must reach screen readers without stealing focus
Do: Use role=status or aria-live=polite for save and filter results
Don't: Silent updates that leave screen reader users unaware
Code Bad: A toast div with no live region

Guideline: Meet WCAG 2.2 target size and focus visibility
Description: Interactive controls need at least 24x24 CSS pixels (44px preferred), and focus must not be hidden behind sticky headers
Do: Keep a 2px visible focus ring and scroll padding under sticky bars
Don't: outline: none with no replacement and focus trapped under a fixed header
Code Bad: button:focus { outline: none; }

Guideline: Use a real icon set, never emoji
Description: Emoji render inconsistently and are announced unpredictably by screen readers
Do: Use an SVG icon component from the project's icon library with aria-hidden or a label
Don't: Emoji as status, navigation or action icons
Code Bad: ✅ Saved

Guideline: Respect high-contrast and forced-colors modes
Description: System forced colors override author colors; borders and focus indicators must survive
Do: Use system colors in forced-colors and keep non-color affordances
Don't: Communicating selection only with background color
Code Bad: A selected row with only a light blue background

Guideline: Prefer C# and Blazor APIs over JavaScript
Description: Most UI behavior has a Blazor equivalent; reach for interop only for browser APIs or an existing JS library
Do: Use C# events, forms, navigation and CSS for interactions
Don't: Rebuilding the component tree in jQuery or manipulating classes from JS
Code Bad: IJSRuntime.InvokeVoidAsync("$('.row').addClass('active')")

Guideline: Load JavaScript as modules and dispose references
Description: ES modules keep scripts isolated and IJSObjectReference lets the component release them
Do: Import a module in OnAfterRenderAsync and dispose it with the component
Don't: Global script tags that leak handlers between navigations
Code Bad: window.chart = new Chart(...) never cleaned up

Guideline: Call interop after the first render
Description: During prerender there is no browser; DOM and window APIs only exist after OnAfterRenderAsync
Do: Guard with firstRender and handle the case where the component is disposed before completion
Don't: Calling localStorage or getBoundingClientRect in OnInitializedAsync
Code Good: protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender) { if (!firstRender) return; ... }
Code Bad: await JS.InvokeVoidAsync("scrollTo", 0) in OnInitializedAsync

Guideline: Never mutate Blazor-owned DOM nodes
Description: Blazor diffs the DOM it renders; external mutations cause lost state and rendering errors
Do: Render the markup in Razor and let JS measure or animate only where Blazor does not own the tree
Don't: Removing or inserting children of a Blazor-rendered element from JavaScript
Code Good: Interop returns a measurement used by C# state
Code Bad: JS removes a Blazor-rendered row and Blazor later throws on diff

Guideline: Virtualize large collections
Description: Virtualize<TItem> renders only the visible window, keeping long grids and logs responsive
Do: Wrap the item container in Virtualize with a stable Items provider and item size estimate
Don't: Rendering 10,000 rows in a plain foreach
Code Bad: @foreach (var row in _allRows) { <OrderRow Item="row" /> }

Guideline: Choose the render mode for cost and latency
Description: Interactive Server reduces download but holds a circuit per user; WebAssembly removes server round trips but costs startup; static SSR costs neither
Do: Match the mode to data locality, latency and scale requirements
Don't: Defaulting every page to Interactive Server or WebAssembly without measurement
Code Good: Static SSR for catalog pages, InteractiveServer for the admin workspace
Code Bad: InteractiveWebAssembly on a low-end mobile marketing page

Guideline: Avoid unnecessary rerenders
Description: A parent rerender re-renders children unless parameters are unchanged or ShouldRender returns false
Do: Keep parameter values stable, use @key and ShouldRender for expensive subtrees
Don't: Wrapping the whole page in a timer-driven StateHasChanged
Code Bad: InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged) from a one-second timer for static data

Guideline: Stream async data with explicit loading states
Description: Long queries should render a skeleton immediately and fill regions as data arrives
Do: Await multiple tasks and render each region when ready
Don't: Blocking the first render on every query combined
Code Bad: await Task.WhenAll(all queries) before rendering anything

Guideline: Optimize WebAssembly download size
Description: Startup time is dominated by the payload a browser must fetch before the app becomes interactive
Do: Trim unused assemblies, lazy-load assemblies and show a first-load progress indicator
Don't: Shipping the full server-side dependency graph to WebAssembly
Code Bad: Referencing the entire EF Core and server pipeline from a WebAssembly client

Guideline: Read the project references before recommending a library
Description: The installed component library defines theme APIs, markup and accessibility behavior; adding another duplicates weight
Do: Inspect .csproj PackageReference, App.razor providers and existing theme files first
Don't: Introducing MudBlazor into a Radzen app to build one dialog
Code Good: PackageReference Include="MudBlazor" conditionally styling with its own theme
Code Bad: Two component libraries imported in the same _Imports.razor

Guideline: MudBlazor: theme with MudTheme instead of ad-hoc CSS
Description: MudThemeProvider and MudTheme define palette, typography, spacing and shadows for every MudBlazor component
Do: Provide a MudTheme in the layout and toggle dark mode with MudThemeProvider.IsDarkMode
Don't: Editing .mud-* CSS classes to change brand colors
Code Bad: .mud-palette-primary { color: #2563eb !important; }

Guideline: MudBlazor: map design tokens into palette and dark palette
Description: PaletteLight and PaletteDark should receive the generated design system colors so components match the token file
Do: Set Primary, Secondary, Background, Surface, TextPrimary, Error and Success from design tokens
Don't: Leaving MudBlazor defaults while the rest of the app uses a different palette
Code Bad: Default purple MudBlazor palette with a blue native header

Guideline: Radzen: register a theme and use RadzenDataGrid features
Description: RadzenTheme selects a built-in theme and RadzenDataGrid provides sorting, filtering, paging and virtualization
Do: Use RadzenTheme in App.razor or the layout and configure the grid's LoadData for server paging
Don't: Building a table from divs beside an installed Radzen grid
Code Bad: <table> hand-rolled next to unused Radzen components

Guideline: Fluent UI Blazor: use FluentDesignTheme and design tokens
Description: FluentDesignTheme applies the Fluent 2 token system, including accent, neutral layers and typography
Do: Configure FluentDesignTheme once and consume its CSS variables in custom components
Don't: Overriding .fluent-* selectors per page
Code Bad: A custom accent color applied with page-level style overrides

Guideline: Commercial libraries need version-specific APIs
Description: Syncfusion, Telerik and DevExpress ship frequent releases with renamed parameters and theme packages; verify against the installed version
Do: Read the package version and that version's documentation before generating component markup
Don't: Copying snippets from a newer major version into an older package
Code Good: Syncfusion SfGrid with AllowPaging and a matching theme stylesheet for the installed version
Code Bad: Telerik parameters that do not exist in the project's installed major

Guideline: Blazorise needs its provider and design system
Description: Blazorise components depend on a Blazorise provider configured with a design system such as Bootstrap or Material
Do: Register AddBlazorise with a design system and add the matching provider in the layout
Don't: Using Blazorise components without a provider and expecting default styles
Code Bad: <Button Color="Color.Primary" /> with no provider registered

Guideline: Do not mix component libraries without an architectural decision
Description: Two libraries mean two theme systems, duplicate accessibility semantics and conflicting CSS resets
Do: Pick one primary library and wrap any exception behind a small project component
Don't: Adding a second library for one chart, drawer or date picker
Code Good: One primary library plus a project-owned wrapper for the exception
Code Bad: MudDialog, RadzenDialog and a native <dialog> in the same app

Guideline: Native HTML components remain valid
Description: Not every button needs a library; plain elements keep bundle size and upgrade risk low
Do: Use native elements with the token system for simple controls
Don't: Adding a dependency for a checkbox or a link
Code Bad: A new component package added for one radio group

Guideline: Treat MAUI Blazor Hybrid as a separate design profile
Description: BlazorWebView renders inside a native app on Android, iOS, Windows and macOS; web-only assumptions break
Do: Target touch, native navigation, safe areas and device capabilities; skip render modes and circuits
Don't: Applying web SSR or render-mode rules to a Hybrid page
Code Bad: @rendermode InteractiveServer inside a MAUI content page

Guideline: Handle safe areas, touch and the soft keyboard
Description: Hybrid layouts sit under notches, home indicators and on-screen keyboards
Do: Use safe-area padding tokens, 44px targets and scroll-into-view when the keyboard opens
Don't: Fixed bottom bars hidden by the keyboard or the home indicator
Code Bad: A fixed footer with bottom: 0 and no safe-area inset

Guideline: Plan offline data and native capabilities
Description: Hybrid apps must survive offline use and expose camera, files and notifications through abstractions
Do: Define device-service interfaces in shared code and implement them per platform
Don't: Calling web APIs directly from UI components and failing offline
Code Bad: Components calling Camera.Default directly and breaking on Windows

Guideline: Set dir and lang at the document root
Description: Direction and language belong on html so layout, fonts and assistive tech agree
Do: Set dir="rtl" lang="fa" for Persian and dir="rtl" lang="ar" for Arabic
Don't: Flipping individual components with transform: scaleX(-1)
Code Bad: <div style="direction: rtl"> around the whole page body

Guideline: Use logical properties in components and tokens
Description: RTL support is a design-system concern; components must mirror without per-page patches
Do: Use margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline and text-align: start
Don't: Left/right hard-coding in isolated CSS
Code Bad: .toolbar { padding-left: 16px; padding-right: 8px; }

Guideline: Mirror directional icons intentionally
Description: Arrows, chevrons, back buttons and progress indicators must follow reading direction; logos and media controls must not
Do: Mirror direction-dependent icons via a dir-aware icon component
Don't: Mirroring every icon or none of them
Code Bad: A back arrow that points the wrong way in Persian UI

Guideline: Format dates and numbers for the active culture
Description: Persian, Arabic and Hebrew interfaces expect localized digits, calendars and plural rules
Do: Set CultureInfo from the request and use ToString with the current culture
Don't: Hard-coded en-US dates and Western digits in a Persian UI
Code Bad: DateTime.Now.ToString("MM/dd/yyyy") everywhere

Guideline: Isolate mixed-direction content
Description: Codes, emails, file paths and numbers inside RTL text need bidi isolation to keep reading order
Do: Wrap LTR fragments in bdi or use unicode-bidi: isolate
Don't: Relying on browser heuristics for order numbers inside Persian sentences
Code Bad: Order INV-2026-0042 rendered with reversed punctuation

Guideline: Test components with bUnit
Description: bUnit renders components in memory and asserts markup, events and parameters without a browser
Do: Cover form validation, permission rendering and grid empty states
Don't: Only testing through manual clicks in the running app
Code Good: var cut = RenderComponent<OrderRow>(p => p.Add(x => x.Item, order));
Code Bad: A test suite that only drives the full app through a browser

Guideline: Verify each render mode end to end
Description: Static SSR, Server, WebAssembly and Hybrid fail differently; a passing build does not prove interaction works
Do: Exercise forms, navigation and auth in the modes the app actually uses
Don't: Testing only the default development render mode
Code Good: Playwright run against the app with the production render mode enabled
Code Bad: Claiming a WebAssembly page works because dotnet build passed
